resources.string:
The Android Id of your device is now in your clipboard!
You can paste it in any application, or use the button below to send it dirrectly.

Warning: It seems you are running the application in an emulator or are affected by a known bug in older Android versions.
You can find more about this in the "Info" Section.

ANDROID_ID is a value used to uniquely identify your Android installation.

It is generated automatically when you start your device for the first time, and it remains constant for the lifetime of the device.

Because the value of ANDROID_ID is re-generated on the device factory reset, it can not be used to reliably identify a certain device.

The value of ANDROID_ID can be also easily changed on rooted devices.

When running in emulator ANDROID_ID has usually the same value: "9774d56d682e549c" (on older SDK emulators the ANDROID_ID value is empty).

On some devices running Android 2.2 there is a bug that makes the ANDROID_ID to be the same for every installation.
